title: An Amateur Astronomer Found an Impact Crater While Looking for a Campsite
mediaSource: Quebec accidental impact crater satellite maps amateur astronomer NASA Earth Observatory

scenes.title: He was looking for a campsite and found a crater
scenes.narration: In Quebec, an amateur astronomer searching online satellite maps for a camping spot noticed a strange circular landform.

scenes.title: The circle turned out to be an impact structure
scenes.narration: What first looked like an ordinary lake or geological feature was later identified as a crater created by an impact event.

scenes.title: The discovery started on a screen
scenes.narration: The first clue did not come from a field expedition. It came from publicly available satellite imagery and the unusual circular outline visible from above.

scenes.title: Satellite images can expose hidden geology
scenes.narration: From space, circular structures and large geological patterns can stand out even when forests, lakes, or rough terrain make them difficult to recognize on the ground.

scenes.title: You do not always need to be a professional to notice something new
scenes.narration: The case shows how open satellite data can allow careful observers outside professional research teams to contribute to real discoveries.

scenes.title: A casual map search became a scientific discovery
scenes.narration: In the age of high-resolution satellite maps, even planning a trip can reveal traces of events that happened deep in Earth's past.
